title: ArcCivs .96 awake-resident food upkeep
assumptions: Explicit sensitivity, not runtime telemetry. Scenarios represent 1/4/6 villages with 5/8/12 adults present and awake for 1/2/4 active hours per village-day. Before working fractions are 0.2/0.5/1; after includes awake idle residents.

One hunger per active awake adult-minute and one existing meal per six hunger remain the steady-state ceiling of ten meals per awake hour. Initial saturation and unavailable food may reduce actual consumption. Sleeping, unrendered/inactive time and offline time are excluded from this estimate. Children lose one hunger per two observed awake minutes; a complete 40-minute childhood can consume at most three meals from initially full hunger.

Native BREAD and Auto abstract FOOD are alternative settlement modes, not two charges on one village. Each meal burns one already existing unit and restores at most six resident hunger; no food items, stock, currency or work credit are created.

A full farmer reserve may legitimately pause production until sufficient room is available; consumption is not increased artificially to keep the farmer working. Existing production quantities and capacities remain unchanged.

Finite progression extension: no currency, player XP or production-rate multiplier changes. 20 paid work cycles formerly grant 20 profession XP; matching stable aptitude grants up to40, bounded by active home cap10/20/30/40. Existing higher XP is retained. One40-active-minute childhood can gain at most10 education XP through observed mentor lessons; it transfers once at adulthood. These are finite character progression windows, not repeatable daily income. Full skill cap remains40 and maximum health28; childhood education alone can raise health20 to22 after adulthood. SELL and future contracts stay separate and unchanged.

For calculator comparison only, one finite full childhood /20 paid-cycle window is modeled per participant-day in all three columns. That is an explicit upper event sensitivity, not a claim of birth frequency; multiply by observed events after activation. Normal food and AutoFOOD rows remain alternative modes, and the finite child rows must not be added to adult rows for the same resident-minute. No new material output quantities or durable item supplies are granted.
